ei.title: The Origin of Miracle: Our Ignorance or Defining as a Miracle
ei.subject: 11월_2023 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: The Origin of Miracle: Our Ignorance or Defining as a Miracle

fullPassage: Coincidence that is statistically impossible seems to us like an irrational event, and some define it as a miracle. But, as Montaigne has said, "the origin of a miracle is in our ignorance, at the level of our knowledge of nature, and not in nature itself." Glorious miracles have been later on discovered to be obedience to the laws of nature or a technological development that was not widely known at the time. As the German poet, Goethe, phrased it: "Things that are mysterious are not yet miracles." The miracle assumes the intervention of a "higher power" in its occurrence that is beyond human capability to grasp. Yet there are methodical and simple ways to "cause a miracle" without divine revelation and inspiration. Instead of checking it out, investigating and finding the source of the event, we define it as a miracle. The miracle, then, is the excuse of those who are too lazy to think.

questions.passage: Coincidence that is statistically (A)[impossible / inevitable] seems to us like an irrational event, and some define it as a miracle. Glorious miracles have been later on discovered to be obedience to the laws of nature or a technological development that was not widely known at the time. As the German poet, Goethe, phrased it: "Things that are mysterious are not yet miracles." The miracle assumes the intervention of a "higher power" in its occurrence that is beyond human capability to grasp. Yet there are (C)[methodical / chaotic] and simple ways to "cause a miracle" without divine revelation and inspiration. Instead of checking it out, investigating and finding the source of the event, we define it as a miracle. The miracle, then, is the excuse of those who are too lazy to think.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

④ impossible — ignorance — chaotic(혼란스러운): (C) 오답
det.tip: impossible(불가능한), ignorance(무지), methodical(체계적인)

questions.passage: Coincidence that is statistically ①<u>impossible</u> seems to us like an irrational event, and some define it as a miracle. det.analysis:
① impossible: 통계적으로 '불가능한' 우연 — 적절
② intelligence(지능) → ignorance(무지): 기적의 기원이 우리의 '무지'에 있다는 맥락에서 intelligence는 반대 의미 ←정답
③ discovered: 자연법칙에 따른 것으로 '발견'되었다 — 적절
④ laws: 자연의 '법칙'에 대한 복종 — 적절
det.tip: ignorance(무지) ↔ intelligence(지능). 기적의 원인은 우리의 무지

questions.passage: Coincidence that is statistically impossible seems to us like an irrational event, and some define it as a miracle. But, as Montaigne has said, "the origin of a miracle is in our ignorance, at the level of our knowledge of nature, and not in nature itself." Glorious miracles have been later on discovered to be obedience to the laws of nature or a technological development that was not widely known at the time. As the German poet, Goethe, phrased it: "Things that are ①<u>mysterious</u> are not yet miracles." The miracle assumes the ②<u>intervention</u> of a "higher power" in its occurrence that is beyond human capability to ③<u>grasp</u>. Yet there are methodical and simple ways to "cause a miracle" without divine revelation and inspiration. Instead of checking it out, investigating and finding the source of the event, we define it as a miracle. The miracle, then, is the excuse of those who are too ④<u>eager</u> to think.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① mysterious: 신비한 것은 아직 기적이 아니다 — 적절
② intervention: '더 높은 힘'의 '개입'을 가정한다 — 적절
③ grasp: 인간의 이해력을 '파악'할 수 없다 — 적절
④ eager(열망하는) → lazy(게으른): 생각하기 너무 '게으른' 사람들의 변명이라는 맥락에서 eager는 반대 의미 ←정답
det.tip: lazy(게으른) ↔ eager(열망하는). 기적은 생각하기 게으른 사람의 변명
